question: Does a 30 W chip stay under 85 C with a 10 CFM, 20 Pa fan blowing along the fins in a 40 C cabinet?
headline: Hottest point reaches 77 C (limit 85 C) at (30, 29.9, 0) mm at steady state.
confidence_reasons: hand calculation: heat balance on a uniform skin gives 69.2 C; the FEA skin averages 72.6 C (12% of the rise). Biot 0.00013: the part is nearly isothermal

checks.name: mesh convergence
checks.summary: temperature rise at the hottest point settled: 37.1 -> 36.9 -> 37 C over 3 meshes, last change 0.4%

checks.name: energy balance
checks.summary: heat in 30 W, heat out through the surfaces 30 W (1.1e-07% apart)

checks.name: hand calculation
checks.summary: heat balance on a uniform skin gives 69.2 C; the FEA skin averages 72.6 C (12% of the rise). Biot 0.00013: the part is nearly isothermal

checks.name: units and sanity
checks.summary: temperatures between 70.7 and 77 C; radiation is off, it could shed up to about 11.6 W at this temperature (pass --radiation 0.9 for painted or plastic surfaces)

assumptions: Aluminum 6063-T5: conductivity 209 W/(m K), specific heat 900 J/(kg K), density 2700 kg/m3.
Heat enters through bottom and box 17.5,17.5,-1,42.5,42.5,0.5.
Convection uses a fixed film coefficient; real coefficients vary with temperature and airflow.
Surrounding air or coolant at 40 C does not heat up.
Contact resistance between parts and internal airflow are not modeled.

_figures: Temperature with the hottest point marked

notes: Built from heatsink.py with base=6, size=60, fins=9, fin=1.5, fin_height=30.
